outcome: Help bank fraud teams stop high-risk digital payments and mule activity in real time while allowing genuine customers to transact with less friction.
overview: Banks face rising authorised-push-payment scams, account takeover and fast-moving mule networks that static rules cannot keep up with. This solution scores every digital payment in real time by combining transaction, customer, device, beneficiary and behavioural signals, then routes it to approve, challenge, hold or investigate — with an explainable reason code and a full audit record for every intervention. A feedback loop learns from confirmed fraud and investigator decisions. A proof of value runs in 8–12 weeks on historical data before any controlled real-time deployment, targeting lower fraud losses, fewer false positives and faster investigations without adding friction for genuine customers.

benefits.text: Reduce preventable scam and payment-fraud losses by a target 15–30%
benefits.source: Redington BFSI catalogue; consistent with published bank fraud-platform case ranges
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Target range to validate against the customer’s own loss baseline during the PoV — not a guarantee

benefits.text: Cut false-positive alerts by a target 20–40%, lowering review cost and customer friction
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Depends on label quality and signal coverage in the customer’s data

benefits.text: Shorten average fraud-investigation handling time by a target 30% with connected-account views
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Measured against an agreed pre-deployment baseline; workflow adoption required

residency: Deployable in-country on local AWS or Azure regions (e.g. UAE, KSA); transaction data never leaves the customer tenancy in the reference designs

notFor.situation: No real-time payment rails or event feed from the payment switch
notFor.why: The decision engine needs an in-flight payment event to act on; batch-only access can only report fraud after the money has moved

notFor.situation: No confirmed-fraud labels or case history to learn from
notFor.why: Model calibration and the PoV benefit case both depend on labelled outcomes

notFor.situation: Latency budget below ~100 ms end-to-end with no tolerance for a challenge step
notFor.why: The reference designs target sub-300 ms decisions; harder budgets need bespoke engineering outside this offer

scope:
Model: Joint delivery: accredited implementation partner leads, with Redington architecture and commercial governance; the customer owns fraud policy and model-risk approval · Duration: 8–12 weeks historical PoV; further 8–10 weeks to controlled real-time launch
Delivery pod: Partner delivery lead + project manager, vendor platform specialist, data scientist; customer fraud owner, payments lead, data owner, model-risk reviewer, security approver · Support model: Business-hours or 24×7 option; severity-based response targets; partner service desk with vendor escalation
1) Discovery and baseline agreement
2) Design and data preparation
3) Historical model build and validation
4) Real-time integration and UAT
5) Training and controlled launch
6) Stabilisation and handover
